name: GlzButton
semanticRole: Execute a clearly labeled user action with one dominant semantic intent.

material.rule: Use the glaze variant only for floating or spatially contextual actions; ordinary content actions remain solid or raised. Danger expresses destructive semantics, not decoration.

input.keyboard: Enter or Space activates the focused button exactly once; activation must not wait for animation.
input.focus: Visible focus ring is at least as discoverable as hover and remains visible in high contrast and forced colors.
input.hover: Pointer hover may add a 3–6% state layer and restrained elevation without changing label or geometry.
input.press: Pressed feedback begins immediately and uses the shared pressed state layer without layout shift.
input.selection: Selected is used only when the action legitimately represents a retained toggle-like state; otherwise omit selected semantics.

accessibility.name: Accessible name comes from the visible action label or an equivalent programmatic name.
accessibility.state: Disabled, loading, selected where applicable, error, and success states are programmatically exposed without color-only meaning.
accessibility.value: No value is required for ordinary action buttons; progress/value is exposed separately when a loading operation has measurable progress.
accessibility.keyboard: Fully operable with keyboard and switch-access activation semantics.
accessibility.focus: Focus is never removed for visual cleanliness and returns predictably after transient overlays invoked by the button close.
accessibility.errorAssociation: If an action error requires explanation, associate the error message with the action or resulting status region.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Replace spring/scale flourish with immediate or short opacity/state feedback.
accessibility.reducedTransparency: Glaze variant resolves to an opaque raised surface while preserving hierarchy.
accessibility.increasedContrast: Strengthen boundary and focus treatment; danger retains explicit label/icon semantics.
accessibility.forcedColors: Use platform ButtonFace/ButtonText/Highlight semantics and preserve destructive text/icon meaning.
accessibility.largeText: Allow labels to grow or wrap where necessary; do not truncate the only action name.

fallbacks.reducedMotion: Short state change with no nonessential scale or spring.
fallbacks.highContrast: Stronger edge, focus ring, and explicit semantic state.
fallbacks.forcedColors: Platform colors and system focus/selection semantics.
fallbacks.performance: Remove optional blur, shadow complexity, and decorative specular effects before changing layout or meaning.

content.overflow: Keep labels stable during loading/success transitions; prefer semantic resizing or controlled wrapping over clipping.
content.localization: Loading and success labels remain meaningful, for example Save → Saving… → Saved, with stable width where practical.
content.rtl: Leading/trailing icon placement mirrors semantically; directional icons mirror only when their meaning is directional.

criteria: Primary action is visually dominant without excessive saturated area.
All five variants remain clearly related members of one component family.
Loading and Saved transitions do not produce distracting layout shift.
Compact pointer sizes retain an accessible hit area without appearing touch-inflated on desktop.
